items.title: Ron Carter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: When I got to New York and went down to Birdland as Chico was working, the cello player decided to stay but the bass player, Bull Ruther, decided to go back to Seattle which was his home. So he's looking for a bass player.

ctx.x: Yeah. He was honest, he was blunt, you know. While it wasn't a new feeling to have .. to hear this, it was kind of a drag because you'd put all this time in in this industry, call it orchestra playing, and to hear that one of the items on the hiring peoples' list is what race you are, it just seems to be what a waste of effort and energy on their part. It seems to me that music sounds great when great players play them. Whatever color they are. But when you are eighteen, you don't think that philosophically; you…

items.title: Ron Carter interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: the first gig I had on the road was at a club at Detroit that’s called the Club Saturn, with Chico Hamilton’s band

ctx.x: When you moved to Detroit, was there a healthy jazz scene in Detroit at that time?

Oh yeah. There were three or four major clubs that brought in major acts. And when I left Detroit and went away to school, the first gig I had on the road was at a club at Detroit that’s called the Club Saturn, with Chico Hamilton’s band; and cross town was Ahmad Jamal’s band and about eight blocks away was T-Bone Walker, the great blues guitarist, and of course the local musicians always had four or five little small places to play so jazz was really alive and well. We’re talking about ’55 through probably ’65,…
How about at Eastman? Was there a recognized jazz program at Eastman when you were there?

items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I gave him his first gig. He was on the band when Eric Dolphy was on the band

ctx.x: Yeah. It’s strange he never said -- you know, all the stuff you read about Ron Carter, I took him right out -- we graduated from Eastman College, man. I gave him his first gig. He was on the band when Eric Dolphy was on the band, you know. But anyway, let’s leave it here. I’ll tell you about -- these guys, you know, are making me famous.
Yeah, making you famous. So the original quintet was going to be Jim Hall on guitar, your drums, Carson -­
